sections.h2: How would you describe Margate's setting?
sections.html:
Margate is in Broward County and was created as the Town of Margate on May 30, 1955, then took city status in 1961. The city's area page puts it at about nine square miles with 30 miles of canals, 7.5 miles from the Atlantic and roughly 20 minutes from Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport and Port Everglades.

The name is said to come from the founder's surname and the word gateway, because the town was seen as a gateway to western Broward. The city provides its own police, fire and emergency medical services, water, wastewater and stormwater service, and it counts 19 parks and recreational facilities including the Calypso Cove aquatics site. Northwest Medical Center and the city itself are among the major employers listed.

Its Community Redevelopment Agency dates to 1996. The same page reports a median age of 46.4 and 2.48 people per household, using older figures, so treat them as background and not as a market reading.

  • Margate runs its own water and sewer, so request a final meter reading from the city at closing.
  • Canal frontage and distance to the coast are worth stating in a listing.
  • A buyer from outside Florida may ask about insurance, so gather your policy details.

sections.h2: Can I still sell a Margate house after a foreclosure suit starts?
sections.html:
You can sell before a court sale takes the house, and Florida's process often leaves a wider window than owners expect. The lender sues in Broward County, wins a final judgment, and only then does the clerk schedule an auction.

Once judgment is entered, the sale date must land 35 days out at the latest and 20 days out at the earliest, absent the lender's consent to a later date (s. 45.031). Notice is published for two consecutive weeks, the top bidder leaves a deposit, and an objection period of 10 days follows the certificate of sale. Under s. 702.10 a lender can seek a faster order to show cause, but a granted homestead exemption on the latest roll creates a presumption of owner occupancy, which keeps a Margate homeowner on the ordinary track.

  • Read every court paper and note the response deadline printed on it.
  • Ask your servicer for a payoff figure in writing.
  • Call a Florida foreclosure attorney or legal aid office early.

sections.h2: What happens to extra money if a Margate house sells at auction?
sections.html:
Whatever remains after the lender and liens are paid is surplus, and the owner can claim it through the clerk. The judgment carries a notice about it, and homestead owners are told to check in within 10 days.

Claims have to be filed before the clerk reports the money as unclaimed. A voluntary sale on your terms usually leaves more control, because the closing agent pays off the mortgage and hands you the balance.

sections.h2: Which months carry a Margate tax discount?
sections.html:
Bills arrive in November, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Paying early earns a sliding discount.

Early-payment discounts on a Broward tax bill
Month paidDiscount
November4 percent
December3 percent
January2 percent
February1 percent

Relief exists for owners who are short of cash. A homestead owner short of the full amount can file Form DR-570 for deferral by the March 31 after the assessment year, covering the part above 5 percent of last year's household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Installment prepayment needs an application to the tax collector by May 1 (s. 197.222).

sections.h2: How do tax certificates and tax deeds threaten a Margate owner who stops paying?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate, sold by June 1 to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest, in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). The certificate holder is barred from pressing the owner for payment during the first two years, counted from April 1 of the year of issue.

After that, a tax deed application can be filed for a $75 fee (s. 197.502). The clerk runs the auction, and on homestead land the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value. Before listing, ask the Broward tax collector whether any certificate is attached to the parcel.

sections.h2: What should I gather before talking to a Margate buyer?
sections.html:
Collect the papers that answer a buyer's first questions, so the offer reflects the real condition of the house. Missing papers are a common cause of a late closing.

  • The mortgage statement with a current payoff figure.
  • Court papers, if a foreclosure suit has been filed, with the case deadlines marked.
  • Your newest tax bill, plus a note of any certificate on the parcel.
  • Any homestead exemption notice from the property appraiser.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since all owners must sign.

Florida requires a land transfer to be written and signed in front of two witnesses, and witnessing may happen by audio-video technology (s. 689.01). Plan signing early when an owner lives out of state. For exemption questions, the Broward County Property Appraiser lists 954-357-6830, open weekdays.

sections.h2: Which offers suit a Margate owner in a hurry?
sections.html:
A cash purchase makes sense when a court date, a tax certificate or a lien sets the pace. It removes financing and appraisal delay, and repairs become the buyer's job.

Get the closing date, the payoff and each fee on paper first. Ask whether the deposit can be refunded, who picks the title company, and how a request for more time would be handled. Sellers who compare two or three written offers, with the same lines filled in, tend to spot the weak ones fast.

If you plan to stay a few weeks after closing, ask for a short rent-back in writing, with a daily rate and a move-out date. Take photos of the house at handover so both sides agree on its condition.

sections.h2: Which Margate services might matter to a buyer or an older seller?
sections.html:
The city area page describes two special districts tied to the commission: the Northwest Focal Point Senior Center, which serves adults age 60 and older in the city and county, and the Community Redevelopment Agency created in 1996. Programs listed for seniors include transportation, an eldercare advocate, home energy assistance and meals.

An older owner who is selling to move closer to family can ask the center about the help on offer before the move. Buyers who are retirees may ask about those services, and the city also points to a fire department rated ISO Class I and recognition for its police department. Cite those points only as the city states them, and let a buyer check the details.

Median household income and age figures on the page are older estimates, so do not quote them as current. Stick to facts you can confirm with the city and keep the listing description plain, so that a buyer's own research matches what you wrote.

faqs.q: What is the gap between foreclosure judgment and auction?
faqs.a: The clerk schedules the sale 20 to 35 days after judgment unless the lender consents to a later date (s. 45.031).

faqs.q: Can I get surplus money after a foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if any remains after liens and the judgment. File a claim with the clerk before the funds are reported as unclaimed.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean I lose my house right away?
faqs.a: No. A deed application cannot be filed until two years have run from April 1 of the issue year (s. 197.502). Ask the Broward tax collector what clearing it would cost.

faqs.q: How does the Florida tax deferral work?
faqs.a: The owner files Form DR-570 with the tax collector, deferring the part above 5 percent of last year's household income.

faqs.q: Who provides water and sewer in Margate?
faqs.a: The city's area page lists water, wastewater and stormwater among its own services.
